      Methodology & Notes

      1. Points Earned is net of "Points Earning Reversed" (order cancellations reversing an earn event before it settles).
      2. Points Redeemed is net of "Redeemed Points Reimbursed" (returns/cancellations of orders that used points).
      3. Redemption Rate = Net Points Redeemed ÷ Net Points Earned for the range shown (a liability-based rate, distinct from the code-issuance rate on the Monthly Overview tab).
      4. LY 6/26/25 shows Points Earned of ~34.8M vs. a ~700K–1.1M daily average (~35–50x) — flagged as a likely bulk adjustment/one-time event rather than organic earning. The "Adjusted" figures exclude that single day (when it falls inside the selected LY range) for a more like-for-like comparison; all other figures are "as reported."
      5. LY July shows a much larger version of the same pattern: six separate days (7/9, 7/10, 7/17, 7/19, 7/20, 7/21/25) each show Points Earned 25–50x the daily average, together accounting for roughly 90% of July's reported LY Points Earned; a single day (7/23/25) accounts for roughly 92% of July's reported LY Points Expired (~37.0M). Unlike 6/26/25, these are not excluded from the "Adjusted" figures — all July LY totals are shown as-reported, per request. Treat LY July's headline Earned/Expired totals as reflecting these concentrated events rather than typical day-to-day activity.
      6. TY Points Expired = 0 is expected, not a performance signal: the current platform launched 5/26/26 with points expiring 12 months from earn, and all pre-migration balances were reset to expire no earlier than 5/26/27. LY (Yotpo) used a 6-month expiration window, so LY naturally shows expiry activity that TY cannot yet show.
      7. LY redemption mechanics (Yotpo) allowed $10 increments up to $50; TY (current platform) allows any amount up to $50 on a sliding scale — redemption counts are not directly comparable at the transaction-size level.
      8. Use the date pickers above to compare custom windows. TY is bounded to 06/01/26–09/30/26 and LY to 06/02/25–09/30/25 — the ranges the source exports cover.
      9. Source files: TY — "Faherty Reports - June (1).xlsx" and "August Rediem Reports.xlsx" (both Liability By Date; the latter, despite its filename, covers July 2026 TY data), "Faherty Reports August 2026 1.xlsx" (Liability By Date, Earning History, and Redemption History for 08/01/26–08/31/26 TY), and "Faherty Reports - September 2026.xlsx" (Liability By Date, Earning History, and Redemption History for 09/01/26–09/30/26 TY). LY — "LY_Yotpo_Liability.numbers" (06/02/25–07/01/25), "LY_July_Liability.numbers" (07/01/25–07/31/25; its duplicated 7/1/25 row was dropped when combining), "LY_August_Liability.xlsx" (08/01/25–08/31/25), and "LY_September_Liability.xlsx" (09/01/25–09/30/25). Note: the LY August and September Earning and Redemptions files were also supplied but aren't used here — the LY side of this dashboard tracks liability totals only, not the earn/redeem category-and-channel breakdowns TY shows (LY never had that breakdown built).
      10. TY's earn/redeem category breakdown for August and September groups actions the same way June–July were grouped, with additions: "Promotions & Bonus Events" (the August "Double Stamps for Parks Week" and September "Fall New Arrivals: Double Stamps" campaigns, which didn't exist in June–July) and, for September, "Other (0 pts)" (zero-point "earn" and "Mobile order return" activity records). Earning is dated by the date the points were created, which ties exactly to the daily Liability By Date totals. "Unique customers earning/redeeming" figures use a fresh customer-ID mapping for each of August and September activity (the earlier raw transaction files aren't available to this dashboard to cross-reference), so a custom date range spanning across a July/August or August/September boundary may slightly overcount repeat customers as new; single-month views are unaffected. On 09/24/26 the Liability By Date report classifies 800 points as non-code redemptions that the Redemption History lists as Order Discounts; totals are unaffected.
